passage:
A teacher saved student projects in an online archive. Years later, students could look back at their early work.
Some laughed at their old mistakes. Others were proud of how much they had improved.
The teacher said the archive was not for judging the past. It was for seeing growth.
One student noticed that his first science report was messy but full of curiosity. His later reports were cleaner, but sometimes less bold. He decided to bring more curiosity back.
The archive showed that progress is not always a straight line. Looking back can teach people what they gained and what they should not lose.
